hindi: अब इसलिए हम लङ्घनबृंहणीय नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter named Laṅghanabṛṃhaṇīya (on lightening and nourishing).
notes: Prose opening formula, typed as a verse unit in the input. The title word is formed from laṅghana and bṛṃhaṇa with the suffix -īya and is not split into members.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus indeed spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula, typed as a verse unit in the input.

hindi: तप और स्वाध्याय में निरत, अग्निवेश-प्रमुख छह श्रेष्ठ शिष्यों को प्रेरित करते हुए आत्रेय ने कहा —
english: Urging them on, Ātreya spoke to his six best disciples, headed by Agniveśa, who were devoted to austerity and self-study:

text_flags.why: possible typo: the word must agree with ātreyaḥ uktavān as masc. nom. sg. present participle (paricodayan); an accusative paricodayam has nothing to agree with, and nothing at the end of the line causes n to become m.

notes: The words spoken follow in unit 4. uktavān (past active participle) is used as a finite verb 'spoke'.

hindi: जो समय पर लङ्घन, बृंहण, रूक्षण, स्नेहन तथा स्वेदन और स्तम्भन को जानता है, वह सचमुच वैद्य है।
english: He who knows lightening (laṅghana), nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa), drying (rūkṣaṇa), oleation (snehana), and also sweating (svedana) and checking (stambhana), at the proper time, he truly is a physician.
notes: kāle 'at the proper time' may go with knowing the measures (knowing them for the right time) or with their use; the literal order is kept. stambhana is rendered 'checking' (making firm, arresting).
lines_deva: लङ्घनं बृंहणं काले रूक्षणं स्नेहनं तथा
स्वेदनं स्तम्भनं चैव जानीते यः स वै भिषक्
lines_iast: laṅghanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ kāle rūkṣaṇaṃ snehanaṃ tathā
svedanaṃ stambhanaṃ caiva jānīte yaḥ sa vai bhiṣak

hindi: कह चुके उन आत्रेय से अग्निवेश ने कहा —
english: To Ātreya, who had spoken, Agniveśa said:
notes: agniveśa uvāca: the visarga of agniveśaḥ is dropped before the vowel u.

hindi: हे भगवन्, लङ्घन क्या है और लङ्घन के योग्य कैसे होते हैं? बृंहण और बृंहण के योग्य, तथा रूक्षण के योग्य और रूक्षण (क्या हैं)?
english: O venerable one, what is lightening, and of what kind are those to be lightened? (What are) nourishing and those to be nourished, those to be dried and drying?
notes: bhagavaṃl laṅghanam: final n of bhagavan becomes nasalised l before l. The question continues in units 7 and 8.

hindi: कौन-से स्नेह हैं और कौन स्नेहन के योग्य हैं, कौन-से स्वेद और कौन स्वेदन के योग्य माने गए हैं, स्तम्भन और स्तम्भन के योग्य — यह आप बताएँ, हे गुरो!
english: Which are the unctuous substances and who are those to be oleated; which are considered the sweating procedures and who are those to be sweated; checking and those to be checked — that you should tell, O teacher!
notes: In the second line stambhanam and stambhanīyāḥ are taken as objects of vaktum together with tat; stambhanīyāḥ could also be nominative like the first line. svedya may be from the causative (svedayati).
lines_deva: के स्नेहाः स्नेहनीयाश्च स्वेदाः स्वेद्याश्च के मताः
lines_iast: ke snehāḥ snehanīyāśca svedāḥ svedyāśca ke matāḥ

hindi: और लङ्घन आदि इन छहों के (ठीक) किए गए, न किए गए और अति किए गए होने का लक्षण संक्षेप में आप बताएँ।
english: And you should tell in brief the sign of these six, beginning with lightening, when done, not done and overdone.
notes: kṛta 'done' is understood as properly done, in contrast with akṛta and ativṛtta.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., indef. pron. (with yat)

hindi: अग्निवेश के उस वचन को सुनकर गुरु ने कहा — जो कुछ शरीर में लघुता उत्पन्न करता है, वह लङ्घन माना गया है।
english: Having heard those words of Agniveśa, the teacher said: Whatever produces lightness in the body is known as lightening (laṅghana).
notes: kiñcil lāghava-: final t of kiñcit becomes l before l.

hindi: और जो शरीर की बृहत्ता उत्पन्न करे, वह बृंहण है; जो रूक्षता, खरता और विशदता करे, वह रूक्षण है।
english: And that which would produce largeness of the body is nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa); that which would cause dryness, roughness and non-sliminess is indeed drying (rūkṣaṇa).
notes: yaccharīrasya = yat śarīrasya (t + ś becomes cch). vaiśadya is the abstract noun of viśada 'non-slimy'.
lines_deva: रौक्ष्यं खरत्वं वैशद्यं यत् कुर्यात्तद्धि रूक्षणम्
lines_iast: raukṣyaṃ kharatvaṃ vaiśadyaṃ yat kuryāttaddhi rūkṣaṇam

words.gloss: producing unctuousness, liquefaction, softness and moisture
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)
n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: स्नेहन वह है जो स्नेह, विष्यन्द, मृदुता और क्लेद उत्पन्न करे; स्वेदन वह है जो स्तम्भ, गुरुता और शीत को नष्ट करे और स्वेद उत्पन्न करे।
english: Oleation (snehana) is what produces unctuousness, liquefaction (viṣyanda), softness and moisture; sweating (svedana) is what removes stiffness, heaviness and cold and produces sweat.
notes: viṣyanda literally 'flowing, oozing'; rendered 'liquefaction'.

hindi: स्तम्भन वह है जो गतिशील और चल को निश्चित रूप से रोक दे। जो द्रव्य लघु, उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, विशद, रूक्ष, सूक्ष्म, खर, सर
english: Checking (stambhana) is that which certainly arrests what is moving and mobile. A substance that is light (laghu), hot, sharp, non-slimy, dry, subtle, rough, flowing (sara),
notes: gatimantam and calam are masculine accusative with no noun expressed; rendered 'what is moving and mobile'. dhruvam is taken as the adverb 'certainly'; it could instead be predicative ('makes the moving, mobile thing firm'). The second line begins the description of lightening substances, which ends in unit 13. GROUPING: the sense runs across the edition's verse numbers: 12b + 13a (lightening substance), 13b + 14a (nourishing), 14b + 15a (drying), 15b + 15c (oleating); the edition's numbering is kept.

hindi: और कठिन हो, वह द्रव्य प्रायः लङ्घन माना गया है। जो द्रव्य गुरु, शीत, मृदु, स्निग्ध, बहल, स्थूल, पिच्छिल,
english: and hard, is generally known as lightening. A substance that is heavy (guru), cold, soft, unctuous, thick, gross, slimy,
notes: The first line completes the list begun in unit 12; the second line begins the description of nourishing substances, which ends in unit 14. See the GROUPING note at unit 12.
lines_deva: गुरु शीतं मृदु स्निग्धं बहलं स्थूलपिच्छिलम्
lines_iast: guru śītaṃ mṛdu snigdhaṃ bahalaṃ sthūlapicchilam

hindi: प्रायः मन्द, स्थिर और श्लक्ष्ण हो, वह द्रव्य बृंहण कहलाता है। जो द्रव्य रूक्ष, लघु, खर, तीक्ष्ण, उष्ण, स्थिर, अपिच्छिल
english: mostly slow, stable and smooth — such a substance is called nourishing. A substance that is dry, light, rough, sharp, hot, stable, non-slimy,
notes: prāyaḥ 'mostly' may qualify the whole list or only the following words; it is placed as in the Sanskrit. The second line begins the description of drying substances, which ends in unit 15. See the GROUPING note at unit 12.
lines_deva: प्रायो मन्दं स्थिरं श्लक्ष्णं द्रव्यं बृंहणमुच्यते
lines_iast: prāyo mandaṃ sthiraṃ ślakṣṇaṃ dravyaṃ bṛṃhaṇamucyate

hindi: और प्रायः कठिन हो, वह द्रव्य रूक्षण है। जो द्रव्य द्रव, सूक्ष्म, सर, स्निग्ध, पिच्छिल, गुरु, शीतल, प्रायः मन्द और मृदु हो, वह स्नेहन माना गया है।
english: and mostly hard — that substance is indeed drying. A substance that is liquid, subtle, flowing, unctuous, slimy, heavy, cold, mostly slow and soft is considered oleating (snehana).
notes: The first line completes the list begun in unit 14; lines b and c form one sentence. See the GROUPING note at unit 12.
lines_deva: प्रायशः कठिनं चैव यद्द्रव्यं तद्धि रूक्षणम्
द्रवं सूक्ष्मं सरं स्निग्धं पिच्छिलं गुरु शीतलम्
प्रायो मन्दं मृदु च यद्द्रव्यं तत्स्नेहनं मतम्
lines_iast: prāyaśaḥ kaṭhinaṃ caiva yaddravyaṃ taddhi rūkṣaṇam
dravaṃ sūkṣmaṃ saraṃ snigdhaṃ picchilaṃ guru śītalam
prāyo mandaṃ mṛdu ca yaddravyaṃ tatsnehanaṃ matam

hindi: जो द्रव्य प्रायः उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, सर, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष, सूक्ष्म, द्रव, स्थिर और गुरु हो, वह स्वेदन कहलाता है।
english: A substance that is mostly hot, sharp, flowing, unctuous, dry, subtle, liquid, stable and heavy is indeed called sweating (svedana).
notes: The list as printed contains both snigdha 'unctuous' and rūkṣa 'dry' (and both sara 'flowing' and sthira 'stable'); prāyaḥ 'mostly' suggests that not every quality is needed in every sweating substance.
lines_deva: उष्णं तीक्ष्णं सरं स्निग्धं रूक्षं सूक्ष्मं द्रवं स्थिरम्
द्रव्यं गुरु च यत् प्रायस्तद्धि स्वेदनमुच्यते
lines_iast: uṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ saraṃ snigdhaṃ rūkṣaṃ sūkṣmaṃ dravaṃ sthiram
dravyaṃ guru ca yat prāyastaddhi svedanamucyate

hindi: जो द्रव्य शीत, मन्द, मृदु, श्लक्ष्ण, रूक्ष, सूक्ष्म, द्रव, स्थिर और लघु बताया गया है, वह प्रायः स्तम्भन माना गया है।
english: A substance described as cold, slow, soft, smooth, dry, subtle, liquid, stable and light is generally known as checking (stambhana).
lines_deva: शीतं मन्दं मृदु श्लक्ष्णं रूक्षं सूक्ष्मं द्रवं स्थिरम्
यद्द्रव्यं लघु चोद्दिष्टं प्रायस्तत् स्तम्भनं स्मृतम्
lines_iast: śītaṃ mandaṃ mṛdu ślakṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ sūkṣmaṃ dravaṃ sthiram
yaddravyaṃ laghu coddiṣṭaṃ prāyastat stambhanaṃ smṛtam

hindi: चार प्रकार की संशुद्धि, पिपासा, मारुत और धूप, पाचन, उपवास और व्यायाम — यह लङ्घन है।
english: Purification of four kinds, thirst, wind and sun, digestives (pācana), fasting and exercise — this is lightening.
notes: The four kinds of purification are not listed in this unit. pipāsā 'thirst' here means enduring thirst; unit 22 speaks of pipāsānigraha, suppression of thirst. māruta here is the physical wind (exposure to wind), as in unit 23.

words.gloss: having abundant Kapha, Pitta, blood and waste

hindi: जिनमें श्लेष्मा, पित्त, रक्त और मल बहुत बढ़े हुए हों, जिनका मारुत उनसे संसृष्ट हो, जो बड़े शरीर वाले और बलवान् हों, वे विशुद्धियों द्वारा लङ्घन के योग्य हैं।
english: Those who have abundant Kapha (śleṣman), Pitta, blood and waste, whose Vāta (māruta) is combined (with these), who are large-bodied and strong, are to be lightened by purifications.
notes: saṃsṛṣṭa-māruta 'whose Vāta is combined' (with the other doṣas named) is the most literal reading. asra = blood.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: vomiting, diarrhoea, heart disease, visūcī, alasaka and fever

hindi: जिनके कफ और पित्त से उत्पन्न रोग मध्य बल वाले हों — वमि, अतीसार, हृद्रोग, विसूची, अलसक, ज्वर,
english: Those whose diseases arisen from Kapha and Pitta are of medium strength — vomiting, diarrhoea (atīsāra), heart disease, visūcī, alasaka, fever,
notes: The sentence continues into unit 21. atīsāra is printed with long ī (also in unit 33); it is the same word as atisāra and the metre is correct, so no flag. visūcī and alasaka are kept as Sanskrit names.

words.gloss: obstruction, heaviness, belching, nausea, loss of taste and the like

hindi: विबन्ध, गौरव, उद्गार, हृल्लास, अरोचक आदि — उनकी चिकित्सा बुद्धिमान् वैद्य प्रायः आरम्भ में पाचनों से करे।
english: obstruction (vibandha), heaviness, belching, nausea (hṛllāsa), loss of taste (arocaka) and the like — them the wise physician should generally treat at first with digestives (pācana).
notes: Continues unit 20. tān 'them' may refer to the patients (yeṣām) or to the diseases (rogāḥ, masculine); both fit.

hindi: जिनके ये ही बताए गए रोग अल्प बल वाले हों, उनके उन रोगों को पिपासा को रोकने और उपवासों से जीते।
english: Those in whom these very diseases, as described, are of slight strength — their diseases one should overcome by suppression of thirst and by fasts.
notes: eta eva = ete eva (final e becomes a before a vowel). teṣām 'of them' (the patients) with tān 'them' (the diseases).

hindi: मध्य बल वाले रोगों को व्यायाम, धूप और मारुत से जीते; तो फिर उन बलवानों के विषय में क्या कहना, जिनके रोगों का बल अल्प हो।
english: One should overcome diseases of medium strength by exercise, sun and wind; what then (need be said) of the strong whose diseases are of low strength?
notes: kiṃ punaḥ 'what then (of)': the measures apply all the more to strong patients whose diseases are weak. The unit does not say in which patients the diseases of medium strength are found.

words.gloss: of those who have urinated much
of those taking unctuous, channel-clogging and nourishing (things)

hindi: त्वचा के दोष वालों, प्रमीढों, स्निग्ध, अभिष्यन्दी और बृंहण द्रव्य लेने वालों के लिए, और वात-विकार वालों के लिए भी, शिशिर में लङ्घन प्रशस्त है।
english: For those with skin disorders, those who have urinated much (pramīḍha), those taking unctuous, channel-clogging (abhiṣyandin) and nourishing (things), lightening is commended in Śiśira — even for those with Vāta disorders.
notes: snigdha-abhiṣyandi-bṛṃhiṇām is a possessive -in form over the whole compound; it may also be read 'of those fattened by unctuous and channel-clogging (food)'. The noun 'things/food' is understood. Śiśira is the late-winter season. api 'even' goes with vātavikāriṇām.

words.gloss: of wild animals, fish and birds

hindi: बिना लेप लगे शस्त्र से बींधे गए, अक्लिष्ट, उचित आयु वाले, सात्म्य स्थान में विचरने वाले मृगों, मछलियों और पक्षियों का मांस बृंहण कहलाता है।
english: The meat of wild animals (mṛga), fish and birds that move in their suitable (habitat) — shot with a weapon that is not smeared, not exhausted, and of the right age — is called nourishing.
notes: digdha 'smeared' is said of a weapon smeared with poison; the translation keeps the literal 'not smeared'. vayastha literally 'standing in (proper) age'. sātmya-cārin literally 'moving in what is suitable'.

words.gloss: constantly given to women and wine
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: क्षीण, क्षत, कृश, वृद्ध, दुर्बल, नित्य मार्ग चलने वाले, नित्य स्त्री और मद्य में आसक्त मनुष्य, तथा ग्रीष्म में, बृंहण के योग्य माने गए हैं।
english: The depleted, the injured, the emaciated, the old, the weak, those constantly travelling, and those constantly given to women and wine are known as men to be nourished, and in Grīṣma.
notes: grīṣme ca 'and in Grīṣma' (the hot season): nourishing is also indicated in that season. madya = wine (intoxicating drink).
lines_deva: क्षीणाः क्षताः कृशा वृद्धा दुर्बला नित्यमध्वगाः
स्त्रीमद्यनित्या ग्रीष्मे च बृंहणीया नराः स्मृताः
lines_iast: kṣīṇāḥ kṣatāḥ kṛśā vṛddhā durbalā nityamadhvagāḥ
strīmadyanityā grīṣme ca bṛṃhaṇīyā narāḥ smṛtāḥ

hindi: और जो शोष, अर्श और ग्रहणी-दोष रूपी व्याधियों से कृश हो गए हैं, उनके लिए मांसाहारी प्राणियों के मांस के लघु रस बृंहण हैं।
english: And for those who are emaciated by the diseases śoṣa (wasting), arśas and grahaṇī disorder, light juices of the flesh of carnivorous animals are nourishing.
notes: rasa here is meat-juice (māṃsarasa), not taste. śoṣa, arśas and grahaṇī are kept as Sanskrit names. kravyāda 'flesh-eater'.

hindi: स्नान, उत्सादन, निद्रा, मधुर स्नेह-बस्तियाँ, शर्करा, दूध और घी — इन्हें सबके लिए बृंहण जानो।
english: Bathing, rubbing with unguents (utsādana), sleep, sweet unctuous enemas, sugar, milk and ghee — know (these) as nourishing for all.

text_flags.why: possible typo: buddhi is a bare stem with no case ending and no role in the sentence, which has no verb; viddhi 'know' (2 sg. impv. √vid) supplies the verb, takes bṛṃhaṇam as predicate accusative, and keeps the metre (same syllable weights).

notes: Translated with the suggested viddhi. Taken as printed, buddhi 'intellect' would give no clear sentence; a reading 'nourishing the intellect' would need a compound buddhibṛṃhaṇam or a case form, which the print does not show.

hindi: कटु, तिक्त और कषाय रसों का सेवन, स्त्रियों के प्रति असंयम, तथा खली, पिण्याक, तक्र और मधु आदि का सेवन रूक्षण है।
english: Use of pungent, bitter and astringent (tastes), lack of restraint with women, and (use) of khali, oil-cake (piṇyāka), buttermilk, honey and the like is drying.
notes: sevanam governs both genitive groups. The chunk does not state how khali differs from piṇyāka, so khali is kept as Sanskrit.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., ppp. caus. ni-√dṛś

hindi: अभिष्यण्ण महान् दोष, और जो मर्म में स्थित ऊरुस्तम्भ आदि व्याधियाँ हैं, वे रूक्षण के योग्य बताई गई हैं।
english: Great doṣas that are clogged (abhiṣyaṇṇa), and those diseases located in the vital points, beginning with ūrustambha (stiffness of the thighs), are indicated as to be dried.
notes: mahādoṣāḥ may also be a bahuvrīhi 'persons with great doṣas', with abhiṣyaṇṇāḥ describing those persons. ūrustambha is kept as a Sanskrit disease name, glossed literally. abhiṣyaṇṇa is printed with ṇṇ, a normal spelling of this participle.

words.gloss: in the chapter on unctuous substances

hindi: स्नेह और जो मनुष्य स्नेहन के योग्य हैं, स्वेद और जो स्वेदन के योग्य हैं — उन्हें मैंने स्नेह-अध्याय में और स्वेद नामक अध्याय में विस्तार से कह दिया है।
english: The unctuous substances and the men to be oleated, the sweating procedures and the men to be sweated — these have been stated by me in detail in the chapter on unctuous substances and in the one named for sweating.
notes: The two chapters are named only as 'the sneha chapter' and 'the one named sveda'.
lines_deva: स्नेहाः स्नेहयितव्याश्च स्वेदाः स्वेद्याश्च ये नराः
lines_iast: snehāḥ snehayitavyāśca svedāḥ svedyāśca ye narāḥ

hindi: जो औषध द्रव, तनु, असर, शीतल करने वाला, मधुर, तिक्त और कषाय हो, वह सब स्तम्भन है।
english: Whatever medicine is liquid, thin, non-flowing, cooling, sweet, bitter and astringent — all that indeed is checking.
notes: yāvat 'as much as, whatever'. śītīkaraṇa 'making cold' (cvi formation).
lines_deva: स्वादु तिक्तं कषायं च स्तम्भनं सर्वमेव तत्
lines_iast: svādu tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ ca stambhanaṃ sarvameva tat

words.gloss: burnt by Pitta, alkali or fire
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)
m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: suffering from poison or excessive sweating
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)
m. nom. pl., ppp. caus. ni-√dṛś

hindi: जो पित्त, क्षार या अग्नि से दग्ध हैं, जो वमि और अतीसार से पीड़ित हैं, जो विष से या स्वेद के अतियोग से आर्त हैं, वे स्तम्भन के योग्य बताए गए हैं।
english: Those burnt by Pitta, alkali or fire, those afflicted with vomiting and diarrhoea, and those suffering from poison or from excessive sweating are indicated as to be checked.
notes: viṣa-sveda-atiyoga may also be read 'excessive (use of) poison and of sweating', with atiyoga governing both. kṣāra = alkali.

words.gloss: on cleanness of heart, belching, throat and mouth
words.gram: f. loc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: वायु, मूत्र और पुरीष के निकल जाने पर, अंगों में लघुता होने पर, हृदय, उद्गार, कण्ठ और मुख की शुद्धि होने पर, तन्द्रा और क्लम के चले जाने पर,
english: When there is release of wind, urine and faeces, lightness of the limbs, cleanness of the heart, belching, throat and mouth, when drowsiness and exhaustion have gone,
notes: vāta here is the wind released from the body. The sentence continues into unit 35 (locative absolutes ending in kṛtaṃ laṅghanam ādeśyam). 'Cleanness of belching' means clean (pure) eructation.

words.gloss: on the joint arising of hunger and thirst
words.gram: m. loc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: स्वेद आने पर, रुचि होने पर, भूख और प्यास के साथ-साथ उदय होने पर, और अन्तरात्मा के व्यथा-रहित होने पर लङ्घन को (ठीक) किया गया बताना चाहिए।
english: when sweat has arisen, and relish (for food), when hunger and thirst arise together, and when the inner self is free from distress, lightening should be declared (properly) done.
notes: Continues unit 34. ruci 'relish, taste for food'; 'for food' is understood. kṛtam means properly done, as in unit 8.

hindi: पर्वभेद, अङ्गमर्द, कास, मुख का शोष, भूख का नाश, अरुचि, तृष्णा, कानों और आँखों की दुर्बलता,
english: Breaking pain in the joints, body-ache (aṅgamarda), cough, dryness of the mouth, loss of hunger, loss of taste (aruci), thirst, weakness of the ears and eyes,
notes: The list continues into unit 37, which gives the verb (bhavet) and the condition (laṅghane 'tikṛte). śoṣa here is the physical dryness of the mouth.

words.gloss: loss of body, digestive fire and strength
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: बार-बार मन का सम्भ्रम, ऊर्ध्ववात, हृदय में अन्धकार, और देह, अग्नि तथा बल का नाश — ये लङ्घन के अति किए जाने पर होते हैं।
english: frequent confusion of the mind, upward wind (ūrdhvavāta), darkness in the heart, and loss of body, digestive fire (agni) and strength would occur when lightening is overdone.
notes: Continues unit 36. abhīkṣṇam 'frequently' is taken with saṃbhramaḥ. deha-agni-bala-nāśa may also be read 'loss of the body's fire and strength'. bhavet is singular with a list of subjects; the Hindi uses the plural.

words.gloss: freedom from the defects of emaciation

hindi: बल, पुष्टि की प्राप्ति और कृशता के दोषों से मुक्ति — यह बृंहित का लक्षण है; और अत्यधिक बृंहित में अति स्थूलता होती है।
english: Strength, gaining of plumpness and freedom from the defects of emaciation are the sign in one (properly) nourished; and excessive corpulence (sthaulya) in one excessively nourished.
notes: ati stands as a separate word after sthaulyam ('corpulence in excess'). kārśya-doṣa may also be read 'emaciation and (other) defects'.

words.gloss: the sign of done and overdone
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: लङ्घित में जो (ठीक) किए गए और अति किए गए होने का लक्षण है, वह रूक्षित में है। बल प्राप्त होने पर और बताए गए रोगों के जीत लिए जाने पर (व्यक्ति) स्तम्भित होता है।
english: The sign of (properly) done and overdone that holds in one lightened holds indeed in one dried. One would be (properly) checked when strength has been gained and the diseases stated have been overcome.
notes: bale labdhe is a locative absolute; yathoktaiś cāmayair jitaiḥ is instrumental in form but is read in the same way ('with the diseases overcome'). The diseases stated are probably those listed as calling for checking in unit 33.

words.gloss: binding of the heart and of the faeces
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: श्यावता, अंगों की जकड़न, उद्वेग, हनुसंग्रह, और हृदय तथा मल का रुकना — यह अति स्तम्भित का लक्षण होता है।
english: Duskiness, stiffness of the limbs, agitation, hanusaṃgraha, and binding of the heart and of the faeces would be the sign of one over-checked.
notes: hanusaṃgraha is kept as a Sanskrit name with a literal gloss. hṛd-varco-nigraha: one nigraha 'binding, holding back' is said of both the heart and the faeces.

words.gloss: for which these are the remedies

hindi: और संक्षेप में, इन छहों के न किए जाने का लक्षण है — जिन धातुओं की ये औषध हैं, उनका शान्त न होना और उनकी वृद्धि।
english: And in brief, the sign of these six when not done would be the non-subsidence, and indeed the increase, of the dhātus for which these are the remedies.
notes: tat-auṣadha 'having these as remedies' qualifies dhātūnām. dhātu here means the bodily factors that these measures treat; the unit does not name them.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: इस प्रकार सब रोगों के छह उपक्रम ठीक-ठीक कहे गए हैं, जो मात्रा और काल का अनुसरण करते हुए साध्य रोगों को साधने में सिद्ध हैं।
english: Thus the six measures of treatment (upakrama) for all diseases have been properly declared; conforming to measure (mātrā) and time, they are effective in curing the curable.
notes: samyak 'properly' may go with proktāḥ (properly declared) or with the measures themselves.

hindi: और यहाँ यह श्लोक है — दोषों के अनेक प्रकार के संसर्ग के कारण उपक्रम मिश्रित हो जाते हैं, परन्तु वे छह की संख्या का अतिक्रमण नहीं करते, जैसे वात आदि तीन की संख्या का अतिक्रमण नहीं करते।
english: And here there is: Because of the manifold combinations of the doṣas the measures of treatment become mixed; but they do not go beyond six, just as Vāta and the others do not go beyond three.
notes: The lead-in bhavati cātra is a line of the unit. The verb na ativartante is understood again with vātādayaḥ.
lines_deva: षट्त्वं तु नातिवर्तन्ते त्रित्वं वातादयो यथा
lines_iast: ṣaṭtvaṃ tu nātivartante tritvaṃ vātādayo yathā

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक हैं — इस प्रकार इस लङ्घन-अध्याय में भगवान् ने प्रश्नों के अनुसार वे छह उपक्रम समझाए हैं, जिनसे चिकित्सा प्रवृत्त होती है।
english: Here, the verses: Thus in this chapter on lightening the venerable one has expounded, according to the questions, the six measures of treatment by which treatment proceeds.
notes: asmiṃl laṅghana-: final n of asmin becomes nasalised l before l. The summary names the chapter laṅghanādhyāya. Only one summary verse follows the plural ślokāḥ in this unit.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में लङ्घनबृंहणीय नामक बाईसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna), the twenty-second chapter named Laṅghanabṛṃhaṇīya.
notes: Chapter colophon; the Sanskrit has no verb and the translation keeps it verbless.
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने लङ्घनबृंहणीयो नाम द्वाविंशोऽध्यायः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne laṅghanabṛṃhaṇīyo nāma dvāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ
